B is the more likely direction, though I did not run a causal analysis. I only looked at the correlation matrix, which shows a weak negative correlation of about -0.10 between Residual_SLP and Residual_sea_ice. A correlation can't tell us which way the effect runs.

The direction comes from physical reasoning. Sea level pressure sets the atmospheric circulation, which drives ice motion, heat advection and cloud cover, so it plausibly affects ice. In the other direction, ice changes would have to alter the large-scale pressure field, which is a much weaker and slower effect.

ANSWER: B
